info.title: Leverage interfaces
info.summary: The agent, owner and helper interfaces of the Leverage server.
info.description: One server, three interfaces. Agents (tag `agent`) sign in with a seat token, the Mac app (tag `owner`) with a session, and the helper (tag `helper`) with its own token, all as `Authorization: Bearer`. Every call that changes something carries an `Idempotency-Key` header and answers one outcome body: 200 completed, 202 pending, 409 refused. JSON fields are the Data model's column names in snake case. Operations are exactly the registry's `operations`; `x-leverage-caller` and `x-leverage-command` say who may call and which commands of the state table it can run. No subscription login, sign-in token, sign-in link, code or API token appears in any request (Credentials); the only secrets in any response are the four one-time tokens, each returned once by the call that issues it; the token of a seat that connects on its own is returned inside its landing prompt (GA-13).

servers.description: A local installation; the address is the owner's to choose.

get.summary: Waits up to `wait` seconds and answers with one item.
get.description: Does not consume what it returns: the first true item of the precedence table repeats until the seat acts. Of the kinds a seat claims, a job comes before a review and a review before a task, which orders them for a General seat, the one role that claims more than one kind (GA-4).

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for an item, at most 30.

get.summary: Reads the current outcome of a command this seat sent.
get.description: Pending, completed with its result, or refused with its cause. A claim whose saved material is no longer available reads refused with not_eligible. Reading it clears `command` in `GET /v1/next`. A pending command that is ended from outside reads refused with one of RC-17's three codes: task_cancelled when the owner cancels the task; lease_expired when the builder's or the review's lease ends; invalid_state for every other ending, the owner's contract edit, a changed input, a release, a run that stops, a seat removed, disabled or paused, and a hold on a provisional claim (milestone 4 plan section 2.1, rule 11).

get.summary: Answers the agent's instructions for its role and connection.
get.description: The landing prompt tells the agent to read this first, with its token, and to follow it (GA-12). Any signed-in seat may read it, in any state: a disabled or paused seat reads the same text, and its `GET /v1/next` answers `none`. Reading it is not a poll: presence reads `GET /v1/next` only. The HTTP form names the address this request came in on, the calls the role may make and the loop; the MCP form gives the MCP settings and the tools. The text never holds the token.

parameters.name: connection
parameters.description: `http`: the agent works through this interface. `mcp`: through the bundled MCP server, whose settings the text gives.

400.description: 400 `malformed`: an unknown connection, or the Host of an HTTP request cannot be put in a pasted command.

post.summary: Claims the next job: a rule check, a question, an approval or a contract draft.
post.description: The planner claims contract drafts; the orchestrator claims rule checks, questions and approvals. A General seat claims every kind, and only while it holds no task, review or provisional claim and no approved action waits for it; it is not given a check at task.before_ready of a task whose contract it drafted (GA-3, GA-5). No seat is given a check at task.before_ready of a task it added with create_task (UX-13a). A seat holds one job at a time: a seat that already holds a job gets that job again, so a run moved to another credential continues it (milestone 4 plan RD-35, RD-40). Jobs are given out oldest first. Replaying a key writes nothing and only returns material while the seat still holds the job in the current role and project. Otherwise it is refused with not_eligible.

post.summary: Returns the result in the fixed shape for the job's kind, with the tokens and spend it used.
post.description: Each accepted result also writes `cost.reported` with the job as subject. A contract draft's result is the Complete contract command. A result after the job's timeout is discarded. It is refused with invalid_state, and writes nothing, after the job's timeout or for a withdrawn job; with task_cancelled for a cancelled task's job; with not_holder from a seat that does not hold the job (milestone 4 plan RD-41); with forbidden from a seat the owner has turned off, whose job is left to its run timeout (a paused seat's result is accepted).

post.summary: Adds a task to the Backlog and completes its contract, as the Add task form does.
post.description: For an enabled seat whose permissions include Create tasks (caller `creator`; otherwise `forbidden`, also for a seat the owner has turned off, UX-13c; a paused seat may call it). Runs Add task, then Complete contract with the seat as caller, so `task.created`, `task.contract_changed` and `task.ready` name the seat as actor and `task.before_ready` runs unchanged (UX-11). Answers AgentTaskCreated with `ready` or `backlog` once the check answers; a model check answers 202 pending, and `GET /v1/commands/{key}` then answers the same result. A refusal in the first answer means nothing was created. After a 202 the task already exists. A later `task_cancelled` means the owner ended it, while `invalid_state` can mean the owner edited its contract. Leave the existing task with the owner after either refusal. Refused `add_task_limit` at 20 tasks added by the seat in a rolling hour, when the seat's origin task was itself added by a seat, or at 50 open tasks agents added in the workspace (UX-14). 422 `invalid` for a project the seat may not name (UX-11c).

post.summary: Reports the model and effort the agent runs on.
post.description: For a seat that connects on its own (a seat the app runs is refused `forbidden`). Runs change_seat as the seat, which may change only its own model and effort: `seat.changed` is written with the seat as actor, and only when a value changes (UX-9). Each value must be one the model catalog lists for the seat's provider (the join instructions give the list), or null; 422 `invalid` otherwise. Allowed at any time, so an agent that switches model reports again. Not needed before claiming.

post.summary: Issues the landing prompt of a seat that connects on its own, with a new token.
post.description: In one transaction the server issues a new token for a seat that connects on its own and has not landed, stores only its hash in `seats.token_hash`, which ends the token before it, and returns the short prompt with the new token in it, in this response only (GA-13). The prompt names the address this request came in on; the app's is `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, so only an agent on the owner's Mac can land. The Connect sheet calls it right after connect_seat, and asks again with a new key when the first answer was lost. A seat that has not landed holds nothing, so the command gives back nothing. Once the seat has landed (it has polled, or holds a task, a review or a job) it is refused `invalid_state`: to give an agent a new prompt, the owner removes it, which ends its token and gives back its work, and connecting a new one gives the new prompt (UX-2). A repeat with the same key answers the outcome without the token or the text.

200.description: The command completed. The first answer for the key carries the token and the prompt in `result` (LandingPromptIssued); a repeat of the key answers 200 with the same envelope and LandingPromptIssuedRepeated, without either.

post.summary: Issues the seat's fresh token for a `start_seat` request.
post.description: In one transaction the server issues a new token, stores only its hash in `seats.token_hash` (which ends the previous token) and returns the token in this response only. The token is never stored: not in a helper request's result, not in the stored command outcome, never in an event. A repeat with the same key answers the outcome without the token; the helper asks again with a new key, which rotates again.

200.description: The command completed. The first answer for the key carries the token in `result` (SeatTokenPickup); a repeat of the key answers 200 with the same envelope and SeatTokenPickupRepeated, without the token.

post.summary: Reports that a run hit a provider limit.
post.description: Writes `credential.limit_reached` and, when a candidate below is available, `credential.switched`; the events carry this call's Idempotency-Key as `command_id`. With `job_id` set it runs report_job_limit, which reads no task state; with no candidate the job is left to its run timeout. It answers `completed`, and its `result` is null: the helper learns what to do next from get_helper_next (milestone 3 plan HE-8).

With `job_id` set it runs report_job_signed_out, which reads no task state; with no candidate the job is left to its run timeout. It answers `completed`, and its `result` is null: the helper learns what to do next from get_helper_next (milestone 3 plan HE-8).

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: On every call that changes something. A repeat with the same key writes nothing and returns the command's current outcome; the same key with a different body is 422 `key_reused`. Keys are kept for at least 7 days.

BadRequest.description: 400 `malformed`: the request could not be parsed.

Unauthenticated.description: 401 `unauthenticated`: the token is missing, unknown or revoked.

Unprocessable.description: 422 `key_reused` (the same key with a different body) or `invalid` (a body that fails its schema, including a link or work reference carrying sign-in details).

CommandName.description: A command of the state table (registry `commands`).

Refusal.description: Why a command was refused. `code` is a registry refusal; `rule_id` and `reason` are set for `blocked_by_rule`. `reason` is also set for `add_task_limit`: which of the agent's Add task limits was met (UX-14).

TransportError.description: Transport errors (IF-3), outside the registry refusals: 400 malformed, 401 unauthenticated, 404 not_found, 422 key_reused (same key, different body) or invalid (a body that fails its schema, including a link or work reference carrying sign-in details).

CommandOutcome.description: The outcome of one command (IF-4): pending (202), completed (200) with its result, or refused (409) with its cause. Returned again by `GET /v1/commands/{key}`.

result.description: The command's result once completed; null while pending or when refused. Never holds a secret.

PendingOutcome.description: 202: the command met a model-checked gate and waits. The seat learns the outcome from `GET /v1/commands/{key}` or `GET /v1/next`.

RefusedOutcome.description: 409: the command was refused and writes nothing. A refusal because a gate failed is final for its key; the holder sends the command again with a new key.

CompletedOutcome.description: 200 for a command whose result the contract does not shape.

result.description: Nothing worth returning, or a small object named in the operation's description.

NextItem.description: One item (IF-34): its kind and its id. The id is the task, the question or, for `command`, the command's key; null for `review`, `job`, `task` and `none`. `review_id` is set only for `briefing_changed` when the seat holds a review (IF-7). Not consumed: the first true row repeats until the seat acts.

Lease.description: A builder or reviewer lease. A heartbeat moves `lease_due_at`.

Evidence.description: Proof for a criterion: an `https` link or a note locating proof inside the work reference.

imaginarium.description: True for the workspace's Imaginarium project, the one every workspace gets at setup (DB-53, IM-7).

latest_work_reference.description: The work reference of the project's most recently added task that has one and whose content is present, or null. Add task fills "Where the work is" from it when a project is picked (decisions.md, UI-6). Not a column.

WorkspaceSettings.description: Workspace settings. The recovery time ceiling has no value yet.

Seat.description: `credential_id` is set for a seat the app runs and null for a seat that connects on its own. The token hash is never returned. `model` and `effort` are `""` for the tool's default on a seat the app runs, picked from the model catalog (models.json); on a seat that connects on its own they are what it reported with report_model, `""` until it reports (UX-7, UX-9).

wanted_running.description: Set by Start (and by Connect for a seat the app runs), cleared by Stop and Remove; the helper's token issue starts every seat that is wanted running (milestone 2 plan IN-30).

run_credential_id.description: The credential the seat's current run is on: the one its seat token was issued for. Null when the seat has no run (milestone 3 plan HD-3).

run_stop_reason.description: Why the seat's last run ended, as the helper reported it or as a limit or sign-out report recorded it; null when no run has ended (milestone 3 plan HD-3, HD-10).

ConnectSeatRequest.description: `credential_id` set connects a seat the app runs (it picks its credential and starts it); null connects a seat that connects on its own, whose token comes with its landing prompt (issue_landing_prompt, GA-13). `model` and `effort` are checked against the model catalog for the credential's provider (`""` or null is the tool's default; with it the effort is the tool's default too), and must be empty for a seat that connects on its own, whose provider must be a login provider: 422 `invalid` otherwise (UX-7, UX-8). `permissions` omitted is all on (UX-10).

ChangeSeatRequest.description: Every field is optional; a field equal to the stored value is no change. `permissions` is the whole set; turning `deliver` off gives back the Working task the seat holds (release reason `deliver_turned_off`, UX-11a). `model` and `effort` are checked against the model catalog only when the request sets one of them or a credential of another provider, and a seat that connects on its own takes neither from the owner: 422 `invalid` otherwise (UX-7, UX-8).

SeatTokenPickup.description: The seat's fresh token for a `start_seat` request. Returned once, in this response only. It is stored hashed, never stored in a command outcome, a helper request or an event; a repeat of the key answers SeatTokenPickupRepeated instead.

SeatConnected.description: The new seat. No token: a seat that connects on its own gets one in its landing prompt, a seat the app runs from the helper's issue_seat_token (GA-13).

HelperTokenIssued.description: The helper's token. Returned once, in this response only. It is stored hashed, never stored in a command outcome, a helper request or an event; a repeat of the key answers HelperTokenIssuedRepeated instead.

SignInRequest.description: The owner's sign-in. One owner per installation. The password is the owner's own, sent only here.

OwnerSession.description: The owner's bearer session. Returned once, in this response only. It is stored hashed, never stored in a command outcome, a helper request or an event; a repeat of the key answers OwnerSessionRepeated instead.

Credential.description: Never the secret, the settings folder or the keychain reference: those stay on the owner's Mac.

limited_since.description: When the current or most recent limit began. Cleared when capacity is restored by a reading or Verify. limited_until is when that limit ends, or null when the provider gave no reset time. Limited means limited_since is set and limited_until is null or later than now (milestone 3 plan HE-3).

Figure.description: One figure the provider supplied. Percent used, never percent left. A real zero is 0, not null; a figure not supplied is not shown.

Reset.description: Available resets of one kind. Resets are shown, not spent.

CredentialReading.description: What a provider reported for an account. Figures and times only, never the raw reply or its headers. `resets` null shows a dash. A reading older than 10 minutes shows its age.

observed_at.description: The time the provider's usage was observed. report_reading accepts at most 60 seconds ahead of the server's command time.

LimitReport.description: A run hit a provider limit (IF-28). Exactly one of `task_id`, `review_id` and `job_id` is set. `reset_at` is null when the provider gave none. Never the raw reply.

SignOutReport.description: A login was found signed out during a run (IF-28). Exactly one of `task_id`, `review_id` and `job_id` is set.

AddCredentialRequest.description: The owner supplies the credential id, which the helper keys the secret by. A pasted token goes to the helper and the Keychain on the Mac and is never part of this request. The row is inserted when this command runs, in state signed_out: until the helper reports every check passed it is not an added credential (list_credentials leaves it out, no seat can be given it, no event is written), and a failed add deletes it (milestone 2 plan IN-24). The masked label is made on the Mac. A login may name a model in the catalog, or let the server use the catalog default. Effort is empty for every new credential, and model is empty for API tokens (UX-7). Strength rank is what Handoff uses.

name.description: Add trims surrounding whitespace and requires a nonblank name unique within this provider and kind, including pending adds.

masked_label.description: The same fixed mask for every API token, with no characters of the token. Null for a login.

model.description: The model used when work reaches this credential from another provider; null for the provider's default.

effort.description: The effort used when work reaches this credential from another provider; null for the default.

strength_rank.description: The strength rank of work run on this credential after a handoff from another provider; null when it keeps the seat's.

name.description: Rename trims surrounding whitespace and requires a nonblank name unique within this provider and kind, including pending adds. Keeping the same name completes without an event.

ReorderCredentialsRequest.description: Every added credential id, in the new handoff order. An empty workspace may send an empty order.

InstallToolRequest.description: The owner confirmed what is installed and from where.

HelperCheckResult.description: One check of Add credential or Verify. `failure` is a code, never provider text.

HelperRequestResult.description: What the helper reports for a request. No token, link or code is ever part of it.

plan.description: For run_add_checks and verify on a login: the plan the provider's tool reports; else null.

account_email.description: For run_add_checks and verify on a login: the account email the provider's tool reports; else null. Kept on the credential row, never in an event.

HelperRequest.description: What the server wants done on the Mac. It never holds a seat token or a credential's name: `params` holds the non-secret inputs and `progress` each check's state while it runs (milestone 2 plan IN-22, IN-23).

HelperNext.description: The next request, or null when none came within `wait`.

RunStartedReport.description: A run started on a seat the app runs. Updates liveness only; writes no event.

RunStoppedReport.description: A run stopped. No event; if the seat holds a review, the server releases it (IF-21).

Event.description: One row of the event log, in its column names.

payload.description: Validated against the type's payload schema in payloads/.

EventsPage.description: Committed events of the workspace with `seq` greater than `after_seq`, in `seq` order, at most `limit`. A reader that passes `next_after_seq` back misses nothing and sees no gap fill later.

facts.description: The ids and flags the item names, validated against the item's facts schema in needs_you.json.

detail.description: The access request description or the reason an approval job stopped an action, when available to the owner. This content is absent from event payloads.

InboxPage.description: Open Needs you items; with `after_seq`, only those whose `inbox.opened` has a higher `seq`.

reviewer_seat_exists.description: For a task waiting for a reviewer in a workspace with a General seat, whether any enabled and unpaused seat may review that task independently, before temporary account waits.

inbox_item.description: The task's open Needs you item, or null.

checking.description: A transition of the task is pending and no hold is open (milestone 4 plan RD-27).

check_reason.description: The reason of the failed check behind an open contract_incomplete hold, or null (RD-27).

waits_for_builder.description: The Finishing task has an approved action and no holder.

waits_for_stronger_agent.description: The Ready task has a minimum strength rank.

Board.description: Provisional (IF-18, milestone 2 plan MA-20, MA-29): the Kanban read.

as_of_seq.description: The seq of the last event the read reflects: the rows and this number are one moment of the log (milestone 2 plan MA-20).

reviewer_seat_exists.description: Whether the workspace has a reviewer seat that is not removed. Cards with a task-specific value use their own value.

TaskStep.description: Provisional (IF-18): one step of a task's timeline, in order (milestone 4 plan section 2.3). seconds is closed_at, or the read's as_of for the open step, less opened_at.

RuleCheckAttempt.description: Provisional (IF-18): one attempt of a rule check (milestone 4 plan section 2.3).

TaskRuleCheck.description: Provisional (IF-18): one rule check of the task, in order of creation, with the rule version it ran and its attempts (milestone 4 plan section 2.3, RD-28). queue_seconds and run_seconds are those of its last attempt.

RecoveryTime.description: One recovery time of the task (PRD L703; milestone 3 plan HE-17): from a credential.limit_reached, or a credential.signed_out with a seat, to the moment work on the same piece of work went on. It ends at the credential.switched the starting command wrote (0 seconds), or else at the first later event of that work whose actor is a seat. Computed from events only.

seconds.description: ended_at minus started_at; for an open one, measured to the moment of the read (L322); null when it was not recovered.

ended_by.description: handoff when another credential took over in the command that wrote the start, seat_event when the continuing seat's first event of that work ended it, not_recovered when the task was cancelled or done first, null while it is open.

HelperRequestParams.description: The non-secret inputs of a helper request that the helper has no other way to learn (milestone 2 plan IN-22): the provider and kind of a credential request, the role, provider, model and effort of a seat request, and for a start request the task or review its run continues (milestone 3 plan HD-1), the provider of an install. The credential and the seat are named by the request's own ids. It never holds a credential's name or a token: the database refuses a `name` key and any key ending in `token`.

model.description: The seat's model; null for the tool's default.

effort.description: The seat's effort; null for the tool's default.

review_id.description: A start request's review to continue (milestone 3 plan HD-1, HD-9). At most one of task_id and review_id is set.

InstallOffer.description: For the tool_installed check of a missing tool: what would be installed and from where, or that Leverage cannot install it (milestone 2 plan IN-23, PV-5). `source_url` is an HTTPS address on a host the helper's catalog lists.

HelperCheckProgress.description: One check's state while a request runs (milestone 2 plan IN-23). `failure` is a code, never provider text, and is set only when `state` is `failed`. `install` is set only on tool_installed while it waits for the owner to confirm an install, or when it failed because Leverage cannot install the tool.

IssueLandingPromptRequest.description: The connection the prompt names: `http` sends the agent to `GET /v1/join`, `mcp` to `GET /v1/join?connection=mcp`, whose text gives the MCP settings (GA-12).

LandingPromptIssued.description: The landing prompt of a seat that connects on its own: one short text, made to be pasted whole into an agent, that names the server's address, carries the seat's fresh token and tells the agent to read `GET /v1/join` with it and follow it exactly (GA-13). `seat_token` is the same token, so that the app can check the text holds it and nothing else shaped like a token. Returned once, in this response only. The token is stored hashed, never in a command outcome, a helper request or an event; a repeat of the key answers LandingPromptIssuedRepeated instead.

examples.text: Join Leverage at http://127.0.0.1:3000 with token example-seat-token. Fetch GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/v1/join with header Authorization: Bearer example-seat-token and follow its instructions exactly.

LandingPromptIssuedRepeated.description: The result a repeat of the key answers in place of LandingPromptIssued: the seat and the connection, with no token and no text, which were shown once and never stored. `repeated` tells it apart from a first answer.

LandingPromptIssuedCompleted.description: 200: the command completed. `result` is LandingPromptIssued the first time the key is answered, with the token shown once inside the prompt, and LandingPromptIssuedRepeated for a repeat of the key (L241, IF-4).

result.text: Join Leverage at http://127.0.0.1:3000 with token example-seat-token. Fetch GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/v1/join with header Authorization: Bearer example-seat-token and follow its instructions exactly.

JoinInstructions.description: The agent's whole instructions for its role and connection (GA-12, GA-14), as Markdown in `text`: what to read first (its briefing, before any work on a task or a review); the work loop (long-poll `GET /v1/next?wait=30`, act on the answer, claim, work, heartbeat while it holds a task or a review, submit, and ask again at once, never stopping on its own); what each next kind means; how a stop arrives (a 401: the seat was removed) and that it then stops at once and tells its user; what it may not do, and how it says what it cannot do (release the work, ask a question, fail a review with notes, or pass a job's question to the owner); and every call (HTTP) or the MCP settings and every tool (MCP) its role may make. A General seat's text names no role file and carries the short safety rules a checker needs (GA-2). The text never holds the token: the agent has it from its landing prompt. `permissions` is what the seat may do now (UX-10); the text says the same and lists only the calls the seat may make. `models` is the model catalog's entries for the seat's provider, for a seat that connects on its own to report its model with report_model; null for a seat the app runs.

examples.text: You are connected to Leverage as a general agent. Ask GET /v1/next?wait=30 again as soon as it answers. Never stop this loop on your own.

SeatPermissions.description: What a seat may do (contract decisions UX-10, UX-11a): `work` claims tasks, reviews and jobs its role allows (new work only; held work goes on); `deliver` submits a task for review, and a seat is offered and leased a task only with both `work` and `deliver`; `create` adds a task with create_task. All three are on for a new seat unless the owner turns one off. Action leases read neither `work` nor `deliver`.

CreateTaskRequest.description: An agent's Add task (UX-11): the task goes to the Backlog and its contract is completed in the same call, as the Add task form does, so `task.before_ready` runs. No outward actions, state, minimum strength or budget cap: those stay the owner's (UX-11b). While the seat holds a task, a review or a job, the task goes into that work's project: an omitted or null `project_id` takes it and any other is refused 422 `invalid`; a seat that holds nothing may name any project of the workspace, or none (UX-11c). The criteria end with exactly one review criterion, as Complete contract requires.

AgentTaskCreated.description: The task an agent added and where it stands once its check has answered (UX-11): `ready` when `task.before_ready` passed, `backlog` when it failed (the task keeps its `contract_incomplete` hold and the owner is told, UX-16). Written when the call completes at once, and by the settled check when the call answered 202 pending.

AgentTaskCreatedCompleted.description: 200: the call completed; `result` is AgentTaskCreated. `command` is `add_task`, the first of the two commands the call runs.

ReportModelRequest.description: The model and effort a seat that connects on its own runs on (UX-9), each exactly as the model catalog names it for the seat's provider, or null when the agent cannot tell (a null model needs a null effort). An unlisted value is refused 422 `invalid` with a sentence listing what is accepted, and nothing is stored.

ReportedModel.description: The seat's model and effort as stored; `""` where the agent reported null.

ReportedModelCompleted.description: 200: the report completed; `result` is ReportedModel. `command` is `change_seat`.

CatalogModel.description: One model of the model catalog as the join instructions give it (UX-9): its exact name and the efforts it accepts (empty when none is documented).
